ideas.title: The Pupil Expansion Glitch
ideas.angle: The viewer is instructed to look closely at their own eyes in a mirror or front camera while thinking of someone they like. It reveals how the autonomic nervous system betrays emotions through pupil dilation, forcing a comment about their result.

hook.en: Look at your pupils right now.

ideas.reason: Interactive eye-related challenges have extremely high retention because they require physical movement from the viewer. The 'eye contact' niche is currently booming on TikTok and Reels.
sources: Psychology Today: The Eyes Have It

ideas.title: The Instant Panic Reset
ideas.angle: Shows how splashing ice-cold water on your face or holding a cold pack to your eyes triggers the Mammalian Dive Reflex. It forces the heart rate to drop instantly, acting as a 'biological kill-switch' for anxiety.

hook.en: You have a hidden reset button.

ideas.reason: Bio-hacking and 'vagus nerve' searches are at an all-time high. This provides an immediate, verifiable physical sensation which drives high APV.
sources: National Institute of Health: Mammalian Dive Reflex Study

ideas.title: The Standing Balance Glitch
ideas.angle: An interactive test where the viewer stands on one leg and closes their eyes. They will tip over in seconds because the brain loses visual anchoring. It challenges them to post how many seconds they lasted.

hook.en: Close your eyes and stand up.

ideas.reason: Physical challenges that 'fail' the viewer are comment magnets. This test leverages the 'proprioception' trend where viewers realize how much they rely on sight for basic motor skills.
sources: Harvard Health: The Science of Equilibrium
